chill.title: Catch Your Dinner at Rainbow Trout Farm
chill.description: This old-school Oak Creek Canyon trout farm hands you a pole, points you at spring-fed ponds under the sycamores, and cleans whatever you catch — grills on site if you want to cook it right there.
chill.bonus: Cook your catch on the spot — leaving with it in a cooler is the coward's move.

chill.title: Aura Reading at Center for the New Age
chill.description: Sedona's decades-old metaphysical headquarters across from Tlaquepaque offers aura photography, psychic readings, and crystal consults — either transformative or at minimum fascinatingly weird.
chill.bonus: Go in completely skeptical and genuinely let yourself surrender to the session — no crossed arms, no smirking.

chill.title: Star Gazing at Schnebly Hill Road
chill.description: Drive up the washboard dirt road past the first switchback after dark and you're above the light pollution with some of the darkest skies in central Arizona spread over you.
chill.bonus: Kill all artificial light including your phone for 20 minutes straight and let your eyes fully dark-adapt — then find the Milky Way core.

chill.title: Vortex Meditation at Airport Mesa Saddle
chill.description: Settle into the red rock saddle just below Airport Mesa's summit where the electromagnetic vortex energy draws seekers from around the world for silent morning sits.
chill.bonus: Sit in total silence for 10 uninterrupted minutes and sketch or write whatever comes up — no phone, no exceptions.

chill.title: Sedona Heritage Museum
chill.description: A pioneer homestead in Jordan Historical Park telling the story of Sedona before the resorts — orchards, apple-packing barn, and old Hollywood Westerns.
chill.bonus: Find the exhibit on the Westerns filmed here and name one you have seen.

chill.title: Oak Creek Canyon Scenic Drive
chill.description: The drive up SR 89A through Oak Creek Canyon to the Mogollon Rim switchbacks — pull off at the overlook for one of Arizona's great views.
chill.bonus: Stop at the top-of-the-rim overlook and look back down the whole canyon.

chill.title: Airport Mesa Overlook
chill.description: The mesa-top overlook above town — a short pull-off with a 360° red-rock panorama that turns into the best sunset spot in Sedona.
chill.bonus: Claim a rock ledge thirty minutes before sunset and stay until the color fades.

chill.title: Crescent Moon / Red Rock Crossing
chill.description: The Oak Creek picnic site where Cathedral Rock reflects in the water — the single most photographed view in Sedona, and a perfect spot to do nothing.
chill.bonus: Find the classic Cathedral Rock reflection in the creek and just sit with it.

chill.title: Amitabha Stupa & Peace Park
chill.description: A Buddhist stupa and peace park tucked into the pinyon and red rock in west Sedona — prayer flags, a quiet trail, and a genuinely calm vortex.
chill.bonus: Walk a slow clockwise circle around the stupa without speaking.

chill.title: Sedona Arts Center
chill.description: The uptown hub of Sedona's long-running artist colony — a gallery of local work and the place that has anchored the town's creative side for decades.
chill.bonus: Pick the one local piece you would actually hang at home.

chill.title: Tlaquepaque Arts & Shopping Village
chill.description: A shaded Spanish-colonial village of galleries and courtyards under giant sycamores by Oak Creek — Sedona's most beautiful place to wander.
chill.bonus: Find a courtyard fountain to sit by and watch the light move through the sycamores.

chill.title: Chapel of the Holy Cross
chill.description: The modernist chapel built directly into the red rocks in 1956 — a short walk up to soaring windows and one of the great views in the Southwest.
chill.bonus: Sit inside facing the window wall for a few minutes of actual quiet.

social.title: Runway Sunset Drinks at Mesa Grill
social.description: Perched on the Sedona Airport mesa, Mesa Grill's patio puts you at eye level with landing Cessnas and a 180-degree sweep of red rock going molten at sunset — half aviation bar, half front-row seat.
social.bonus: Time your toast to a landing — glasses up as the wheels touch.

social.title: Sedona International Film Festival Screening
social.description: Running every March since 1994, SIFF brings serious independent cinema to the Mary D. Fisher Theatre with filmmaker Q&As and a surprisingly sharp audience that debates films over wine in the parking lot afterward.
social.bonus: Stay for the Q&A and ask the director or a panelist the most specific craft question you can think of — not a generic compliment.

social.title: Sedona Trolley Historic Tour
social.description: This narrated open-air tram circuit has been orienting visitors to Sedona's geology, Indigenous history, and neighborhood layout since 1996 — better intel than any app, delivered by locals who actually live here.
social.bonus: Ask the driver for their personal favorite trail that isn't on the official tour route — then go hike it tomorrow.

social.title: First Friday Gallery Tour on Gallery Row
social.description: On the first Friday of every month, the galleries along SR-179 — Exposures International to Lanning — pour wine and stay open late while golden hour hits the red rocks between stops.
social.bonus: Walk into a gallery and ask a gallery rep which piece they'd personally take home — then disagree with them.

social.title: Art of Wine
social.description: A cozy tasting room in the Hillside shops pouring Arizona and global wines by the flight — a calm, grown-up alternative to the cantina scene.
social.bonus: Do an Arizona-only flight and see if local wine surprises you.

social.title: Mooney's Irish Pub
social.description: A genuine Irish pub in west Sedona with Guinness on tap and a patio — the closest thing Sedona has to a neighborhood local.
social.bonus: Order a Guinness and settle in for whatever conversation finds you.

social.title: Javelina Cantina
social.description: The uptown cantina with a margarita list and a deck over the creek — loud, fun, and the easiest happy hour with a view in town.
social.bonus: Order a prickly-pear margarita on the deck and toast the rocks.

social.title: Sedona Beer Company
social.description: A west-Sedona brewpub with house beers and a patio aimed straight at the red rocks — burgers, brews, and a sunset backdrop.
social.bonus: Get a patio seat timed to sunset and watch the rocks turn red.

social.title: Sound Bites Grill
social.description: The uptown dinner-and-live-music venue with a celebrity showroom — one of the only real nightlife rooms in a famously early-to-bed town.
social.bonus: Book a show night and stay through the headline set.

social.title: Vino di Sedona
social.description: A laid-back wine and craft-beer bar in west Sedona with a huge list, regular live music, and a patio that stays mellow late.
social.bonus: Catch whoever is playing live and stay for a full set.

social.title: Page Springs Cellars
social.description: The flagship of Arizona wine country, a short drive to Page Springs — Rhône-style wines and a terraced patio over Oak Creek.
social.bonus: Taste the Rhône reds and find the one you would ship a case of home.

social.title: Oak Creek Brewery & Grill
social.description: Sedona's original brewery, with a rooftop grill in the Tlaquepaque area and house beers brewed just down the road — the town's reliable beer stop.
social.bonus: Order a sampler flight and rank the beers before the food arrives.

adventure.title: Bear Mountain Trail
adventure.description: Sedona's toughest maintained trail gains over 1,800 feet in a relentless series of false summits — the payoff is a true summit panorama from the San Francisco Peaks to Cathedral Rock that almost nobody earns.
adventure.bonus: No sitting down until the true summit — the false summits don't count and you know it.

adventure.title: Thunder Mountain Trail
adventure.description: This rugged red-dirt climb beneath Capitol Butte winds through juniper and manzanita to canyon-wall views — and the exact silence everyone comes to Sedona claiming to want.
adventure.bonus: Stop moving completely for two full minutes at the high point and just listen.

adventure.title: Loy Canyon Trail
adventure.description: One of Sedona's longest and least-trafficked canyon hikes winds through riparian corridors and past ancient ruins with almost zero chance of seeing another soul on a weekday.
adventure.bonus: Push all the way to the canyon's back wall and eat your lunch there — no turning around at the first ruin.

adventure.title: Birthing Cave Trail
adventure.description: A short but steep scramble leads to a massive natural sandstone cave used by Sinagua women for centuries, now one of Sedona's most quietly powerful spots.
adventure.bonus: Sit alone inside the cave for five minutes with your back to the opening and describe exactly what you hear.

adventure.title: Honanki Heritage Site
adventure.description: This lesser-visited Sinagua ruin complex on the outskirts of Red Rock country delivers ancient cliff dwellings and sweeping canyon views without the crowds of better-known sites.
adventure.bonus: Count the number of intact doorways visible in the main ruin wall and guess their original purpose before looking it up.

adventure.title: Palatki Heritage Site Cliff Dwellings
adventure.description: Walk directly into 1,000-year-old Sinagua cliff dwellings tucked into a red sandstone alcove, guided by a ranger who knows every petroglyph by name.
adventure.bonus: Find the pictograph panel and identify at least three distinct symbols before the ranger points them out.

adventure.title: Soldier Pass Trail
adventure.description: A west-Sedona trail past the Devil's Kitchen sinkhole and the Seven Sacred Pools to a hidden cave arch above the canyon — a greatest-hits hike.
adventure.bonus: Find the Soldier Pass Cave and climb up inside the arch.

adventure.title: West Fork Trail
adventure.description: The famous canyon hike up Oak Creek Canyon crossing the creek a dozen times between towering walls — the most beautiful trail in the Sedona area, and stunning in fall.
adventure.bonus: Make all the creek crossings without soaking a boot.

adventure.title: Slide Rock State Park
adventure.description: A natural red-rock water chute in Oak Creek Canyon where the creek has carved an 80-foot slide through the sandstone — Arizona's best natural waterslide.
adventure.bonus: Slide the full natural chute at least once, cold water and all.

adventure.title: Pink Jeep Tour — Broken Arrow
adventure.description: The iconic off-road tour that has been crawling the Broken Arrow trail since 1960 — Devil's Staircase, Submarine Rock, and a wild ride over the slickrock.
adventure.bonus: Ride the front seat down the Devil’s Staircase without grabbing the bar.

adventure.title: Devil's Bridge Trail
adventure.description: The hike to the largest natural sandstone arch in Sedona — the payoff is the nerve to walk out onto the span itself.
adventure.bonus: Walk out onto the arch and stand in the middle for one photo.

adventure.title: Cathedral Rock Trail
adventure.description: A short but steep scramble up the slickrock saddle of Sedona's most iconic formation — hands-on rock climbing to a saddle with a jaw-dropping view.
adventure.bonus: Make the saddle and stand in the notch between the spires.

active.title: Bike the Little Horse Trail to Chicken Point
active.description: This flowy singletrack rolls off the Bell Rock Pathway through juniper country to the slickrock overlook at Chicken Point — technical enough to be fun, forgiving enough to clean it, and no shuttle logistics.
active.bonus: Ride the steepest switchback section clean on your first attempt — no dabbing a foot to the ground.

active.title: Oak Creek Swimming Hole at Grasshopper Point
active.description: Locals have been jumping from the flat sandstone ledges into Oak Creek's cold green water at Grasshopper Point for generations — it's free, it's beautiful, and it's the best afternoon move in Sedona.
active.bonus: Jump from the highest ledge where it's safe to do so — no dangling your feet and retreating.

active.title: Snoopy Rock Viewpoint at Margs Draw
active.description: The short connector from Margs Draw trailhead delivers the definitive head-on view of Snoopy Rock silhouette that everyone photographs from the highway but almost no one earns on foot.
active.bonus: Photograph Snoopy Rock from directly below so the profile is unmistakable — post it without explaining what people are looking at.

active.title: Mescal Trail to Tabletop
active.description: This underrated loop climbs to a flat-topped mesa with 360-degree views of Wilson Mountain and Coffeepot Rock that most Sedona visitors never see.
active.bonus: Tag the highest point on the tabletop and take a panorama photo — send it to someone who thinks they've seen all of Sedona.

active.title: Red Rock State Park
active.description: A quieter state park southwest of town with creekside nature trails and a visitor center — guided bird walks and shade along Oak Creek.
active.bonus: Walk the creekside loop and count how many distinct birds you can spot.

active.title: Fay Canyon Trail
active.description: An easy, shaded out-and-back into a red-rock box canyon in west Sedona, with a short spur up to a hidden natural arch.
active.bonus: Find the unmarked spur and scramble up to the hidden Fay Canyon arch.

active.title: Doe Mountain Trail
active.description: A short switchback climb to the flat top of a mesa in west Sedona — a summit you can walk the whole rim of, with 360° views.
active.bonus: Walk the entire mesa rim once you reach the top.

active.title: Templeton Trail
active.description: A scenic connector winding beneath Cathedral Rock along Oak Creek — gentle grades, big views, and a quieter approach to the icon.
active.bonus: Find the spot where Cathedral Rock lines up perfectly above the trail.

active.title: Hiline Trail Mountain Bike
active.description: Sedona's signature mountain-bike trail — exposed slickrock ledges high above the Village of Oak Creek with Cathedral Rock straight ahead.
active.bonus: Clean the exposed ledge section without dabbing a foot.

active.title: Airport Mesa Loop Trail
active.description: A 3.3-mile loop wrapping the base of Airport Mesa with continuous red-rock views in every direction — the all-around-town panorama hike.
active.bonus: Hike the full loop and name every formation you can see along the way.

active.title: Boynton Canyon Trail
active.description: A canyon hike into one of Sedona's most famous vortex sites, ending in a box canyon of red walls and pines — with a side spur up to Kachina Woman.
active.bonus: Take the spur up to the Kachina Woman knoll and feel out the vortex for yourself.

active.title: Bell Rock Pathway
active.description: The easy, mostly flat path circling Bell Rock in the Village of Oak Creek — the gentlest way to get right up against a Sedona formation.
active.bonus: Scramble up the lower slopes of Bell Rock as far as feels safe, then back.

foodie.title: Brunch at Hideaway House
foodie.description: Perched above Oak Creek with a deck that stares straight at Snoopy Rock and Mitten Ridge, this longtime local spot serves dependable Southwestern brunch with a cold beer and no pretense whatsoever.
foodie.bonus: Claim the corner deck table — if it's taken, wait for it.

foodie.title: Dinner at Dahl & DiLuca Ristorante
foodie.description: This West Sedona Italian institution — open since 1995 — packs in locals and knowing visitors nightly for its romantic candlelit room, deep wine list, and zero resort stuffiness.
foodie.bonus: Order the nightly off-menu pasta special and ask your server what wine they'd personally pair with it — then order that bottle.

foodie.title: Tortas de Fuego
foodie.description: The local Mexican spot in west Sedona where the trail crews and crews actually eat — generous tortas, tacos and molcajetes at honest prices.
foodie.bonus: Order a torta the size of your forearm and try to finish it.

foodie.title: Pisa Lisa
foodie.description: Lisa Dahl's wood-fired pizzeria in west Sedona — blistered pies and serious gelato in a louder, more casual room than her grills.
foodie.bonus: Order a pizza and a gelato and decide which one Lisa does better.

foodie.title: Cress on Oak Creek
foodie.description: The fine-dining room at L'Auberge de Sedona set right on the banks of Oak Creek — the splurge dinner, with the creek running past your table.
foodie.bonus: Request a creekside table and let the kitchen choose your courses.

foodie.title: ChocolaTree Organic Eatery
foodie.description: An all-organic vegetarian eatery and garden patio that leans fully into Sedona's wellness side — house chocolate, herbal everything, and a quiet courtyard.
foodie.bonus: Order something you cannot pronounce and finish the whole thing.

foodie.title: Black Cow Café
foodie.description: The uptown ice cream stop famous for its prickly-pear ice cream — the classic walk-and-eat treat on the main drag.
foodie.bonus: Order the prickly-pear flavor and eat it walking uptown, no sitting down.

foodie.title: Indian Gardens Café & Market
foodie.description: A shaded creekside café and market up Oak Creek Canyon — a great turkey-pesto sandwich and a patio under the cottonwoods on the way to the trails.
foodie.bonus: Build a trail picnic from the market and eat it on the creekside patio.

foodie.title: Coffee Pot Restaurant
foodie.description: The west-Sedona breakfast landmark famous for '101 omelettes' beneath Coffee Pot Rock — a true old-Sedona institution.
foodie.bonus: Order an omelette so strange you have to read the menu twice to confirm it.

foodie.title: The Hudson
foodie.description: An elevated American kitchen perched above SR 179 with a deck looking straight at the red rocks — the deviled eggs and the view are the order.
foodie.bonus: Get a deck table and order the deviled eggs before anything else.

foodie.title: Mariposa Latin Inspired Grill
foodie.description: Lisa Dahl's clifftop Latin grill with a wood-fired patio framing the red rocks — the most spectacular dinner view in town.
foodie.bonus: Book the patio at golden hour and time your main course to the sunset.

foodie.title: Elote Café
foodie.description: The most sought-after table in Sedona — elevated regional Mexican that draws a line before it opens. The elote and the lamb adobo are non-negotiable.
foodie.bonus: Get there before the doors open, order the elote, and do not skip the lamb.
